# SSB Consecration — Travel & Stay System

**Live app:** https://ssb-travel-stay.vercel.app
**Traveller ID link format:** `https://ssb-travel-stay.vercel.app/#/id/<token>` (generated by the app, no login needed)

Built 27 Jul 2026 against the *Developer Handoff Specification* and *AppSheet Sheet Blueprint* Google Docs, with the prototype HTML as the visual reference. This is a real web application, not AppSheet: a static front end on Vercel talking to a Postgres database on Supabase.

## Stack and where everything lives

The front end is two files — `index.html` (markup plus all styling) and `app.js` (all behaviour) — deployed to Vercel as static assets. There is no build step and no framework, so editing either file and redeploying is the whole change cycle. The back end is a Supabase project named **hasirushaale** (project ref `zbqetpvgipgagmmyupcn`, region ap-south-1 / Mumbai). Every table, function and storage bucket for this system is prefixed `mkn_` or `mkn-`, so it sits alongside the unrelated `hs_*` tables in that project without touching them. Only the publishable (anon) key is embedded in the front end; all privileged operations go through database functions.

## Roles

Anyone can create an account from the sign-in screen, and every new account lands as **Requester** — able to raise a request for themselves and see nothing else. An **Admin** promotes people from the *Users & Roles* screen. The account `pallerlasuhruth08@gmail.com` is automatically made Admin the first time it signs up; everyone else must be promoted manually.

**Requester** raises a single request for themselves and uploads their own ID inline. **Team POC** additionally gets the bulk table for 10–25 team members or vendors, and hands out a per-traveller ID link instead of collecting IDs. **Coordinator** sees every request, approves or rejects, and edits the reference lists. **Travel Desk** sees approved requests only and records the PNR/seat plus an optional ticket file. **Accommodation Desk** sees approved requests only and assigns a stay location and a bed number from 1 to 200. **Admin** can do all of the above plus assign roles.

## The flow

A request is raised (self-service with an inline ID upload, or by a POC as a table row with the ID delegated to a link). It lands in the **Coordinator Queue** as *Awaiting approval*. Once the coordinator approves, it becomes visible to both backend desks at the same time — they work in parallel and neither blocks the other. When all three parts are done — ID received, stay allocated, travel booked — the request flips to **Confirmed** automatically. That last rule is enforced by the database as a generated column, not by application code, so it cannot drift.

## Data model

`mkn_requests` holds one row per traveller and carries the requester type, POC fields, traveller fields (including age and gender), dates, travel mode/from/to/arrival/last-mile, the conditional travel-detail fields (`train_name`/`train_number`, `flight_name`/`flight_number`, `bus_name` — only the set matching `travel_mode` is populated), the ID fields, the approval fields, and the stay and travel status and allocation fields. `travel_mode` is one of **Train**, **Flight**, or **Bus (general, not organised)** — a plain public/private bus, as opposed to any SSB- or IYC-organised transport. `mkn_profiles` maps each auth user to a role and team. `mkn_teams` and `mkn_stay_locations` are the reference lists, editable from the *Reference Lists* screen without a code change. `mkn_recommended_trains` and `mkn_recommended_flights` still exist in the database but are no longer used by the front end now that travellers enter their own train/flight name and number directly.

Request IDs are sequential (`SSB-4824`, `SSB-4825`, …) rather than random, so they sort chronologically and never collide. A POC batch also gets a shared `batch_id`, and **each traveller in the batch still gets their own request ID and their own ID-upload link** — that resolves the "one link or one ID / one person, yeah" ambiguity in the recording by giving you both.

## Security model

Row-level security is on for every table. A requester can only ever read rows they created. The two desks can read approved rows only, and cannot read anything before approval. Neither desk can write the other's fields — every desk and coordinator action goes through a `SECURITY DEFINER` function (`mkn_approve`, `mkn_set_stay`, `mkn_set_travel`, `mkn_set_role`) that re-checks the caller's role server-side, so a tampered browser cannot bypass it. Users cannot change their own role; a trigger blocks it.

ID handling follows the privacy rule in the spec. The full ID number is written once and never read back by the application — the front end only ever selects `id_number_masked`, which stores `XXXX-XXXX-1234` for Aadhaar. ID images live in a **private** storage bucket and are served only through short-lived signed URLs to authorised staff. Anonymous travellers opening their link get no table access at all; they can call exactly two functions, one to read their own trip summary and one to submit their ID. A link works once — re-use is rejected.

Bed numbers are unique per stay location; a double-booking attempt is rejected by the database with a clear message.

## Known gaps — decide before go-live

The stay locations are placeholders taken from the MKN block names, because the real list was never supplied. Replace them from *Reference Lists*. The recommended train and flight lists are the four-item sample lists from the prototype and need replacing with real options.

There are no notifications yet. The spec suggests emailing the traveller their ID link on POC submit and a confirmation when all three parts are done. Today the POC copies links out of the app and sends them over WhatsApp or email manually.

Handover requires two account transfers: the Vercel project (`ssb-travel-stay` under `suhruth-s-projects`) and the Supabase project (`hasirushaale`). Note that the Supabase project also hosts the unrelated `hs_*` tables, so transferring it hands over both — if that is a problem, the `mkn_*` tables need moving to their own Supabase project first, which requires a paid plan because the free tier caps at two projects per account.

## Redeploying after an edit

Edit `index.html` or `app.js`, then deploy the folder to the existing `ssb-travel-stay` Vercel project. Because there is no build step, what you upload is exactly what runs.
